notes: Replace bigquery-cross-dataset-location-compatibility with bigquery-secondary-replica-write-boundary because Preview global queries complicate a blanket location restriction. Replace gke-autopilot-privileged-workload-restrictions with gke-standard-autopilot-workload-coexistence to avoid repeating b1's privileged-container fact.

cards.statement: HA VPN requires a BGP-capable peer gateway when an architect connects an on-premises network.
cards.explanation: HA VPN uses dynamic BGP routing, so the on-premises VPN gateway needs BGP capability for route exchange.

cards.statement: HA VPN qualifies for an availability SLA when a single gateway interface carries its tunnels.
cards.explanation: An HA VPN gateway with one active interface has no availability SLA. The topology needs redundancy across its interfaces to qualify.
cards.misconception: One active HA VPN gateway interface provides an availability SLA.
cards.volatilityNote: Google can change the topologies that qualify for an HA VPN availability SLA.

cards.statement: Cloud Router automatically manages route exchange while Google's VPC infrastructure forwards application packets.
cards.explanation: Cloud Router operates in the control plane through BGP sessions. Google's Andromeda infrastructure performs packet forwarding.

cards.statement: Google's Partner Interconnect SLA covers the segment between the provider network and the VPC network.
cards.explanation: Google's Partner Interconnect SLA covers the Google-to-provider connection. Coverage for the provider-to-customer segment depends on the provider.
cards.volatilityNote: Google or a connectivity provider can change the scope of contractual availability coverage.

cards.statement: Network Connectivity Center lets a VPC spoke exclude selected subnet ranges from export to its hub.
cards.explanation: Network Connectivity Center provides VPC spoke export filters. Excluding subnet ranges limits which routes that spoke shares with the hub.

cards.statement: VPC Network Peering lets two networks exchange subnet traffic through a mutually peered third network.
cards.explanation: VPC Network Peering connects adjacent peers rather than providing transitive routing. Two networks sharing a peer need another connectivity path between them.
cards.misconception: A shared VPC peer acts as a transit network between its other peers.

cards.statement: A hierarchical firewall policy delegates matching traffic to later policy evaluation with goto_next.
cards.explanation: A matching goto_next rule ends evaluation of its current firewall policy and continues at the next step in policy evaluation. This permits lower-level policy decisions.

cards.statement: Cloud IDS automatically blocks a network flow when its inspection engine detects an intrusion.
cards.explanation: Cloud IDS inspects mirrored traffic and alerts on threats. Enforcement needs a separate control because Cloud IDS takes no action to block an attack.
cards.misconception: Cloud IDS combines threat detection with automatic blocking of the original traffic.

cards.statement: A Cloud Armor policy on a Cloud Run service's load balancer also protects its direct service URL.
cards.explanation: Cloud Armor evaluates requests through the protected load balancer. A client reaching Cloud Run's default URL bypasses that policy, so the design needs ingress restrictions.
cards.misconception: Cloud Armor protection at the load balancer extends to direct Cloud Run URL requests.

cards.statement: Cloud NAT lets a VM accept internet connections initiated by outside clients through the NAT gateway.
cards.explanation: Cloud NAT translates outbound connections and their response traffic. It rejects unsolicited inbound connections, so a public listener needs a different ingress design.
cards.misconception: Cloud NAT's shared external addresses expose VMs to client-initiated inbound connections.

cards.statement: Autoclass automatically promotes a colder Cloud Storage object to Standard storage when an app reads it.
cards.explanation: Autoclass moves an object's data back to Standard storage after a read, so renewed access changes the storage class used for future accesses.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage lets administrators shorten a locked bucket retention policy when retention needs change.
cards.explanation: A locked Cloud Storage retention policy permits a longer retention period, but blocks shortening or removing the policy. Administrators commit to that restriction when locking it.
cards.misconception: An administrator can shorten a bucket's retention period after locking the policy.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage soft delete can recover an overwritten object as a new live version during its retention period.
cards.explanation: Cloud Storage keeps overwritten objects in a soft-deleted state for the retention period. Restoring one creates a new live copy in the same bucket.

cards.statement: Local SSD automatically replicates workload data to preserve it after an unrecoverable host failure.
cards.explanation: Local SSD is attached to the VM's physical host and lacks automatic replication. Host errors can lose its data, so durable recovery needs another copy.
cards.misconception: Local SSD automatically replicates data for durable recovery after host failure.

cards.statement: Compute Engine standard snapshots share unchanged disk blocks by default across a disk's snapshot chain.
cards.explanation: After the first full snapshot, later standard snapshots normally store changed data and reference existing blocks. Compute Engine sometimes captures a fresh full image.

source.title: About archive and standard disk snapshots

cards.statement: Cloud SQL can use its high availability standby to serve application read queries while the primary is healthy.
cards.explanation: A Cloud SQL high availability standby reserves its role for failover rather than serving read queries. A read replica is the design for offloading reads.
cards.misconception: The high availability standby doubles as a read-serving instance while the primary is healthy.

cards.statement: Spanner requires the Enterprise Plus edition for a database with a multi-region instance configuration.
cards.explanation: Spanner places multi-region instance configurations in Enterprise Plus. Selecting that deployment scope therefore affects the edition an architect chooses.
cards.volatilityNote: Google can change the instance configurations included in each Spanner edition.

cards.statement: Bigtable multi-cluster routing provides immediate read-your-writes consistency across replicas by default.
cards.explanation: Bigtable multi-cluster routing offers eventual consistency. A read routed to another cluster may miss a just-completed write while replication catches up.
cards.misconception: Multi-cluster routing makes an acknowledged write immediately visible in each replicated cluster.

cards.statement: BigQuery's secondary dataset replica accepts independent application writes in its own region.
cards.explanation: A BigQuery secondary dataset replica is read-only until promoted to primary. Application writes go to the primary replica.
cards.misconception: A secondary BigQuery dataset replica accepts independent writes alongside the primary.

cards.statement: BigQuery can prune clustered blocks within a partition when a query filters on clustering columns.
cards.explanation: BigQuery maintains clustering within each partition. Clustering-column filters let a query skip irrelevant storage blocks inside the selected partitions.

cards.statement: Compute Engine's autoscaler automatically combines scaling signals using the largest suggested VM count.
cards.explanation: The autoscaler derives a VM count from each scaling signal and selects the largest. This lets a workload scale for whichever bottleneck demands more instances.

source.title: Using an autoscaling policy with multiple signals

cards.statement: Managed instance group autohealing restores application health by rerouting requests to healthy VMs.
cards.explanation: Autohealing recreates VMs whose applications fail the configured health check. Load balancing redirects requests away from unhealthy VMs.
cards.misconception: Autohealing repairs an application by redirecting its traffic rather than recreating its VM.

source.title: Set up an application-based health check and autohealing

cards.statement: Compute Engine can retain a preempted Spot VM with the default stop termination action.
cards.explanation: Spot VMs use stopping as their default termination action. Selecting deletion removes the VM resource when Compute Engine preempts it.

cards.statement: Compute Engine's default sole-tenant maintenance policy confines live migration to a fixed pool of physical servers.
cards.explanation: Compute Engine's Default sole-tenant maintenance policy lets eligible VMs migrate to new physical servers. Migrate within node group confines migration to a fixed server pool.
cards.misconception: The default sole-tenant maintenance policy preserves the fixed physical-server pool needed by some licenses.

cards.statement: GKE keeps a regional cluster's control plane available for management during a single-zone outage.
cards.explanation: GKE places regional control plane replicas in different zones of one region, preserving access to the Kubernetes API during a zone outage.

cards.statement: GKE Standard limits Autopilot mode to workloads deployed in separate clusters.
cards.explanation: A Standard cluster can host Autopilot-managed workloads alongside workloads on manually managed node pools. Teams choose the management scope within the same cluster.
cards.misconception: Autopilot-managed workloads require their own cluster when teams also retain Standard node pools.
cards.volatilityNote: Autopilot integration and supported workload options in Standard clusters continue to evolve.

source.title: About Autopilot mode workloads in GKE Standard

cards.statement: Cloud Run requires a Serverless VPC Access connector for Direct VPC egress to private resources.
cards.explanation: Direct VPC egress sends Cloud Run traffic to the VPC network without a connector. Teams avoid provisioning a connector to reach private resources this way.
cards.misconception: Direct VPC egress still carries private traffic through a Serverless VPC Access connector.

source.title: Direct VPC with a VPC network

cards.statement: A fleet supports GKE clusters from different projects under a shared fleet host project.
cards.explanation: The fleet host project holds the fleet resource, while registered clusters can remain in other projects. This enables management across project boundaries.

cards.statement: Google Cloud VMware Engine lets the default vCenter user keep full administrator privileges permanently.
cards.explanation: VMware Engine's default vCenter user has limited administrative privileges. Administrators temporarily elevate access for advanced tasks.
cards.misconception: The default vCenter account provides permanent full administrative control over the managed private cloud.

cards.statement: VM Manager bases patch compliance on reported OS inventory and the OS distribution's update metadata.
cards.explanation: VM Manager periodically compares VM inventory with distribution update metadata; its dashboard reflects that reported patch state.

cards.statement: Agent Platform Pipelines runs Kubeflow Pipelines SDK workflows on Google-managed infrastructure.
cards.explanation: Agent Platform Pipelines runs compatible Kubeflow Pipelines SDK workflows as a managed service. Google operates the execution infrastructure, reducing the team's cluster-management work.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported pipeline execution features can evolve as Agent Platform changes.

source.title: Introduction to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Pipelines

cards.statement: Agent Platform Pipelines runs tasks with independent inputs sequentially by default within a pipeline run.
cards.explanation: Agent Platform Pipelines runs independent tasks in parallel by default. The workflow DAG's input-output dependencies impose ordering when one task consumes another task's output.
cards.misconception: The order in a pipeline definition forces independent tasks to execute serially.
cards.volatilityNote: Pipeline scheduling defaults and workflow capabilities may change.

source.title: Introduction to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Pipelines

cards.statement: Agent Platform ML Metadata traces a model back to the datasets and runs that produced it.
cards.explanation: Agent Platform ML Metadata records links between artifacts and executions. The lineage graph supports auditing which training data and workflow runs contributed to a model.
tags: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform ML Metadata
cards.volatilityNote: Agent Platform's metadata and lineage capabilities may evolve.

source.title: Introduction to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform ML Metadata

cards.statement: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Model Garden can offer managed APIs or self-deployment for selected open models.
cards.explanation: Model Garden offers managed APIs for selected open models and self-deployment into your Google Cloud project. A model's available serving options determine who provisions its serving infrastructure.
tags: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Model Garden
cards.volatilityNote: Model Garden's model catalog and available serving options change over time.

source.title: Deploy open models from Model Garden

cards.statement: AI Hypercomputer supports GKE orchestration for distributed training across multiple GPU hosts.
cards.explanation: AI Hypercomputer includes GKE as an orchestration option for containerized AI workloads. Architects can retain Kubernetes scheduling while using accelerator infrastructure for large training jobs.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported AI Hypercomputer orchestration and accelerator combinations may evolve.

source.title: Plan and create your AI infrastructure

cards.statement: Compute Engine fulfills a Flex-start MIG resize request incrementally as individual GPUs become available.
cards.explanation: Compute Engine fulfills a Flex-start MIG resize request by creating the VM group together after requested capacity becomes available. This suits training jobs that need their workers at the same time.
cards.misconception: A Flex-start MIG resize request grows its worker group gradually as individual GPUs become available.
cards.volatilityNote: GPU consumption options and provisioning guarantees may change.

source.title: About resize requests in a MIG

cards.statement: Document AI's Form Parser extracts scanned-form tables into structured rows and cells.
cards.explanation: Document AI's Form Parser returns tables as header rows, body rows, and cells. This structured output preserves relationships needed by downstream processing of scanned forms.
cards.volatilityNote: Document AI processor capabilities and supported table structures may change.

cards.statement: Cloud Vision API SafeSearch can score hateful imagery as a separate moderation category.
cards.explanation: Cloud Vision API SafeSearch scores adult, spoof, medical, violence, and racy content. Its categories exclude hate-content classification, so moderation designs need a separate capability for that risk.
cards.misconception: SafeSearch covers hate-content detection as part of its explicit-content classification.
cards.volatilityNote: SafeSearch's available moderation categories may evolve.

cards.statement: Gemini Enterprise uses project IAM grants to override source-document ACLs for ACL-enabled connectors.
cards.explanation: Gemini Enterprise uses source-system ACLs to govern document access through connectors that enforce end-user permissions. Granting Google Cloud IAM access leaves those source permissions in force.
cards.misconception: Project IAM roles replace source-document permissions when a third-party connector enforces ACLs.
cards.volatilityNote: Connector access controls and IAM integration may change as Gemini Enterprise evolves.

source.title: Configure granular access controls for apps and data stores

cards.statement: Gemini Notebook Enterprise can automatically refresh imported Google Docs used for answer grounding.
cards.explanation: Gemini Notebook Enterprise creates a static copy of imported sources for analysis. Its answers use that copy, so a later edit to the original Google Doc does not change the imported content.
cards.misconception: Imported Google Docs remain live-linked for automatic grounding in subsequent document edits.
cards.volatilityNote: Source ingestion and grounding behavior may change as Gemini Notebook Enterprise evolves.
